Which group of people in West Africa with significant populations in Ghana, Ivory Coast, Liberia and Sierra Leone use the Ida?

Plukenetia conophora
0: Plukenetia conophora, also called Nigerian walnut, and conophor, is a climbing shrub in the genus "Plukenetia".
1: It is not related to the walnut, being so named because its nuts bear a superficial resemblance to the walnut.
2: It is native to tropical western and central Africa from Togo to Congo and in Sierra Leone.
3: It is abundant in the Nigeria, Cameroon, Republic of the Congo and Democratic Republic of Congo.
4: It prefers rain-forest hedge in half-shady places; low bush; secondary forest; plantations at elevations from 250-1400 m Although it is well recorded in Sierra Leone, it is apparently not indigenous to Sierra Leone, since it is not recorded in Liberia and Ghana.
5: Its presence in Sierra Leone is due to returning slaves for it is known to the Krio by its Yoruba (Nigerian) name.
6: Plukenetia conophora is the only Plukenetia species native to West Africa or Central Africa.
7: Others Plukenetia species are indigenous to other parts of Africa, the Indian Subcontinent, Southeast Asia, and America.

Project Fame West Africa
0: Project Fame, also known as Project Fame West Africa or MTN Project Fame West Africa (for sponsorship purposes), is a music talent TV reality show filmed in Lagos and aired in the West African subcontinent.
1: It is a regional version of "Star Academy" reality series that was developed and is licensed worldwide by Endemol.
2: The show used to feature contestants from Ghana, Liberia, Nigeria and Sierra Leone, but Liberia and Sierra Leone have been dropped since the 2014 Ebola Outbreak.
3: The show is broadcast by networks in these four countries and across the African continent.

Ida (sword)
0: The Ida is a kind of sword used by the Yoruba people of West Africa.
1: It is a long sword with a narrow to wide blade and sheathe.
2: The sword is sharp, and cuts on contact but typically begins to dull if not sharpened regularly.
3: It can be single-edged or double-edged.
4: These blades are typically heavier by the tip of the blade.

Fula people of Sierra Leone
0: Fula people of Sierra Leone is the third major ethnic group in Sierra Leone and a branch of the Fula people of West Africa.
1: The Fula make up about 10% of Sierra Leone's population.
2: The Sierra Leone Fula people settled in the Western Area region of Sierra Leone more than four hundred years ago as settlers from the Fouta Djallon Kingdom that expanded to northern Sierra Leone (Kabala, Bombali).

Yoruba people
0: The Yoruba share borders with the Bariba to the northwest in Benin, the Nupe to the north and the Ebira to the northeast in central Nigeria.
1: To the east are the Edo, Ẹsan and the Afemai groups in mid-western Nigeria.
2: Adjacent to the Ebira and Edo groups are the related Igala people found in the northeast, on the left bank of the Niger River.
3: To the southwest are the Gbe speaking Mahi, Egun, Fon and Ewe who border Yoruba communities in Benin and Togo.
4: To the southeast are Itsekiri who live in the north-west end of the Niger delta.
5: They are ancestrally related to the Yoruba but chose to maintain a distinct cultural identity.
6: Significant Yoruba populations in other West African countries can be found in Ghana, Ivory Coast, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

Ptychadena tournieri
0: Ptychadena tournieri is a species of frog in the family Ptychadenidae.
1: It is a widespread species in West Africa and found in Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, Sierra Leone, Liberia, and Ivory Coast, as well as in Togo and Benin; it is assumed to occur in Ghana and southeastern Burkina Faso, although it has not been recorded there.
2: On the other hand, some records may refer to other species; the Amphibian Species of the World excludes Gambia and Togo from the distribution.
3: Common names Liberia grassland frog and Tournier's rocket frog are sometimes used.

West Africa
0: West Africa, also called Western Africa and the West of Africa, is the westernmost subregion of Africa.
1: West Africa has been defined as including 18 countries: Benin, Burkina Faso, the island nation of Cape Verde, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, the island of Saint Helena, Senegal, Sierra Leone, São Tomé and Príncipe and Togo.
2: The population of West Africa is estimated at about /1e6 round 0 million people as of .
3: Islam is the predominant religion of 70% of the population, with smaller amounts practicing Christianity and Traditional African religions.

Mohamed Sillah
0: Mohamed Yahya Sillah was born December 12, 1949 in Massam Kpaka, Pujehun District, Republic of Sierra Leone.
1: His father, Alhaji Yahya Sillah, now 100 years old, served as Regent Chief (Acting Paramount Chief) for several years in Dama Chiefdom, Kenema District in the early seventies.
2: Alhaji Yahya Sillah was appointed to that high position by Sierra Leone President Siaka Stevens.
3: His mother, Haja Mamie Zoe Mansaray, was a home maker.
4: A journalist and human rights activist, Mohamed Yahya Sillah was a vocal torch-bearer in the transition efforts from military to civilian rule in Sierra Leone, 1996.
5: As Leader and National Chairman of National Alliance Democratic Party (NADP), he competed the 1996 Presidential elections in Sierra Leone, becoming one of only thirteen political leaders that qualified to contest the Presidential and Parliamentary elections in the country at the age of 46.
6: His adoring personality lured many Sierra Leoneans and media practitioners to view him as one of the most eloquent and charismatic politicians in Sierra Leone.
7: Nevertheless, he received only 0.5% of the votes (3,723 total votes), good for 13th place.
8: Although he protested the election results on BBC's Focus on Africa, he later suspended his protest "for the sake of peace."
9: Mohamed Yahya Sillah continues to enjoy massive support from the youth and women supporters in Sierra Leone.
10: In 2007, he withdrew his bid for national leadership in the Presidential and Parliamentary elections, citing inadequate funding and ineffective campaign management machinery.
11: He later put his weight behind the Sierra Leone Peoples Party (SLPP) presidential candidate, Vice President Solomon Berewa.
12: When Berewa lost the elections, Mohamed Yahya Sillah gracefully congratulated the winning candidate, Ernest Bai Koroma, of the All People's Congress (APC) party.
13: Mohamed Yahya Sillah vows to respect and help protect the dignity of any Sierra Leonean that is legitimately and democratically elected to office by the people of Sierra Leone.

Cocoa production in Ivory Coast
0: Ivory Coast (Côte d'Ivoire) leads the world in production and export of the cocoa beans used in the manufacture of chocolate, as of 2012, supplying 33% of cocoa produced in the world.
1: West Africa collectively supplies two thirds of the world's cocoa crop, with Ivory Coast leading production at 1.8 million tonnes as of 2017, and nearby Ghana, Nigeria, Cameroon and Togo producing additional 1.55 million tonnes.
2: Ivory Coast overtook Ghana as the world's leading producer of cocoa beans in 1978, and today is highly dependent on the crop, which accounts for 40% of national export income.
3: The primary non-African competitor of Ivory Coast is Indonesia, which went from having almost nonexistent domestic cocoa industry in the 1970s to becoming one of the largest producers in the market by the early 2000s.
4: According to the UN FAO, Indonesia overtook Ghana and became the second-largest producer worldwide in 2006.
5: (World Cocoa Foundation provides significantly lower figures for Indonesia, but concurs that it is the largest producer of cocoa beans outside West Africa.)
6: Large chocolate producers such as Cadbury, Hershey's, and Nestle buy Ivorian cocoa futures and options through Euronext whereby world prices are set.

Saro (Nigeria)
0: Saros or "Creoles in Nigeria" during the nineteenth century and early twentieth century were freed slaves who migrated to Nigeria in the beginning of the 1830s.
1: They were known locally as saros (elided form of Sierra Leone, from the Yoruba "sàró") or Amaros: migrants from Brazil and Cuba.
2: Saros and Amaros also settled in other West African countries such as the Gold Coast (Ghana).
3: They were mostly freed and repatriated slaves from various West African and Latin American countries such as Sierra Leone, Brazil and Cuba.
4: Liberated "returnee" Africans from Brazil were more commonly known as "Agudas", from the word "àgùdà" in the Yoruba language.
5: Most of the Latin American returnees or Amaros started migrating to Africa after slavery was abolished on the continent while others from West Africa, or the Saros were recaptured and freed slaves already resident in Sierra Leone.
6: Many of the returnees chose to return to Nigeria for cultural, missionary and economic reasons.
7: Many (if not the greater majority) of them were originally descended from the Yoruba of western and central Nigeria.
8: Other Nigerian groups forming part of the Sierra Leonean Krio population included Efik, Igbos, Hausa and Nupe.

Which dialect spoken in the province of Scania calls Spettekaka, "spiddekaga"?

Baghdad Jewish Arabic
0: Baghdad Jewish Arabic is the Arabic dialect spoken by the Jews of Baghdad and other towns of Southern Iraq.
1: This dialect differs from the dialect spoken by the Jews in Northern Iraq, such as Mosul and 'Ana.
2: The Baghdadi and Northern dialects may be regarded as subvarieties of Judeo-Iraqi Arabic.
3: As with most Judeo-Arab communities, there are likely to be few, if any, speakers of the Judeo-Iraqi Arabic dialects who still reside within Iraq.
4: Rather these dialects have been maintained or are facing critical endangerment within respective Judeo-Iraqi diasporas, namely those of Israel and the United States.
5: In 2014, the film "Farewell Baghdad" (Arabic: مطير الحمام; Hebrew: מפריח היונים, lit.
6: "The Dove Flyer"), which is performed mostly in Jewish Baghdadi Arabic dialect, became the first film to be almost completely performed in Judeo-Iraqi Arabic.

Nagoya dialect
0: The Nagoya dialect (名古屋弁 , Nagoya-ben ) is a Japanese dialect spoken in Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture.
1: In a wide sense, Nagoya dialect means the dialect in the western half of the prefecture (formerly part of Owari Province), and in that case, it is also called Owari dialect (尾張弁 "Owari-ben").
2: The dialect spoken in the eastern half of the prefecture (formerly part of Mikawa Province) is different from Nagoya dialect and called Mikawa dialect (三河弁 "Mikawa-ben").

Mikawa dialect
0: The Mikawa dialect (三河弁 , Mikawa-ben ) is a Japanese dialect spoken in eastern half of Aichi Prefecture, former Mikawa Province.
1: It is subdivided into western variety centered Okazaki and eastern variety centered Toyohashi.
2: The Mikawa dialect is classified into the Gifu-Aichi group of the Tokai-Tosan dialect with the Nagoya dialect spoken in western half of Aichi Prefecture, however the Mikawa dialect also closes to dialects spoken in western Shizuoka Prefecture and southern Nagano Prefecture.

Hakata dialect
0: Hakata dialect (博多弁 , Hakata-ben ) is a Japanese dialect spoken in Fukuoka city.
1: Hakata dialect originated in Hakata commercial district, while a related Fukuoka dialect (福岡弁 , Fukuoka-ben ) was spoken in the central district.
2: Hakata dialect has spread throughout the city and its suburbs.
3: Most of Japanese regard Hakata dialect as the dialect typical of Fukuoka, so it is sometimes called "Fukuoka-ben".

Jiangyin dialect
0: Jiangyin dialect (江阴话) is a Northern Wu Chinese dialect spoken in the city of Jiangyin in Jiangsu province.
1: Jiangyin dialect is a member of the Wu Chinese Taihu Wu family of dialects, which means the inhabitants speak a dialect similar to that of nearby Wuxi, Changzhou, Suzhou, and Shanghai.
2: Jiangyin dialect itself is of the Piling variety, related to the Changzhou dialect.
3: Jiangyin dialect has the highest degree of mutual intelligibility with the dialects of the closest neighboring cities of Changzhou and Wuxi but also has a fairly large degree of mutual intelligibility with the dialects of nearby Suzhou and Shanghai.
4: As one travels south towards Wuxi away from the urban center of Jiangyin, Jiangyin dialect gradually becomes more and more closer sounding to the Wuxi dialect.

Spettekaka
0: Spettekaka or spettkaka ("spiddekaga" in native Scanian) is a local dessert of the southern parts of Sweden, chiefly in the province of Scania (Skåne) but also in Halland.
1: It is an important part of the Scanian culinary heritage.
2: The name means "cake on a spit", and this describes the method of preparation: it is the Swedish variation on the spit cake.

Pahang Malay
0: Pahang Malay (Standard Malay: "Bahasa Melayu Pahang"; Jawi: بهاس ملايو ڤهڠ) is a dialect of Malay language spoken in the Malaysian state of Pahang.
1: It is regarded as the dominant Malay dialect spoken along the vast riverine systems of Pahang, but co-exists with other Malay dialects traditionally spoken in the state.
2: Along the coastline of Pahang, Terengganu Malay is spoken in a narrow strip of sometimes discontiguous fishermen villages and towns.
3: Another dialect spoken in Tioman island is a distinct Malay variant and most closely related to Riau Archipelago Malay subdialect spoken in Natuna and Anambas islands in the South China Sea, together forming a dialect continuum between the Bornean Malay with the Mainland Peninsular/Sumatran Malay.

Scanian dialect
0: Scanian (   ) is a closely related group of South Swedish dialects spoken in the province of Scania in southern Sweden.
1: Scanian formed part of the old Scandinavian dialect continuum and are by most historical linguists considered to be an East Danish dialect group, but due to the modern-era influence from Standard Swedish in the region and because traditional dialectology in the Scandinavian countries normally has not considered isoglosses that cut across state borders, the Scanian dialects have normally been treated as a South Swedish dialect group in Swedish dialect research.
2: However, many of the early Scandinavian linguists, including Adolf Noreen and G. Sjöstedt, classified it as "South Scandinavian", and some linguists, such as Elias Wessén, also considered Old Scanian a separate language, classified apart from both Old Danish and Old Swedish.

Irpinian dialect
0: The Irpinian dialect, or Irpino, is the dialect spoken in almost all of the comuni in the Province of Avellino in the Italian region of Campania.
1: It is a variant of the Neapolitan language but does however differ from pure neapolitan in certain phrases, pronunciation and the use of definite articles.
2: The dialect however is heavily influenced by its geographical neighbours.
3: For example in the northern area of Avellino, there are some undertones of the accent from Benevento.
4: The dialect spoken in Ariano Irpino or the other towns close to the border with Apulia also has a distinct pugliese tone.

Upper Saxon German
0: Upper Saxon (German: "Obersächsisch" ) is an East Central German dialect spoken in much of the modern German State of Saxony and in the adjacent parts of Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia.
1: Though colloquially called "Saxon" ("Sächsisch" ), it is not to be confused with the Low Saxon dialect group in Northern Germany.
2: Upper Saxon is closely linked to the Thuringian dialect spoken in the adjacent areas to the west.
